recipes.name: Creamy Dill Cucumber Toasties
ingredients_raw: 1 (.7 ounce) package dry Italian-style salad dressing mix
1 French baguette, cut into 1/2 inch thick circles

steps.text: In a medium bowl, mix together cream cheese, dressing mix and mayonnaise.
Spread a thin layer of the cream cheese mixture on a slice of bread, and top with a slice of cucumber. Sprinkle with dill. Repeat with remaining ingredients.

raw_recipe.headline: Creamy Dill Cucumber Toasties
raw_recipe.description: This simple but tasty appetizer takes its cue from English tea sandwiches -this time, atop crusty baguette slices with a creamy spread.

review.reviewBody: THANK YOU!!! This recipe was a huge hit at my family reunion, and was SO easy! I used plain Melba Rounds, and splurged on a seedless English Cucumber. It sliced very thinly, which is key in this recipe. I used fresh dill on top; tiny sprigs arranged to look like seagrass. A faint brushing of paprika added the final color. My relatives thought I had been to culinary school! Chilled on a crisp white platter, these make a great addition to any party!

Easy, easy appetizer that makes a nice presentation! I used 1.5 tbsp. of the Italian dressing and scissored some fresh dill in with the mixture. Let it sit in the fridge for part of the day. I took the suggestion from another reviewer and used a carrot grater to slice the cucumber thinly, rolled it on my finger and placed it on the bread. I didn't care for this method because when taking a bite the whole cucumber tended to come right off. So next time I will get a seedless cucumber and put a single slice on top (whether it's round or a decorative flower) or even matchstick strips going vertical would work. I will definitely make this again! It was great with the french baguette, but I will also try pumpernickel and rye to change it up. Also, I did use fresh dill for everything.

I signed up to bring cucumber, cream cheese 50 sandwiches (cut in 1/4s) to my son's school pen pal tea party. Since I couldn't make them the same day of the party, I would make the sandwiches the night before. I couldn't find any recipes that wouldn't make the bread soggy the next day. I tested this recipe several days prior to the party, made a sandwich the night before and had it for lunch the next day. I used honey & milk bread, spreading it on both sides of the bread. The bread wasn't soggy at all. It was just as fresh as if I made it a few minutes earlier. I used 1/2 a packet of seasoning instead of the whole packet. It would be too salty, in my opinion for a full packet. My son liked it better as a dip. I used English cucumbers since they have less seeds and more flavor. It also tastes great on crackers, not premade. After 2 loaves of bread and doubling the filling, the sandwiches were a hit and no sogginess. Thank you. Will make again.

This is an easy appetizer that kids and vegetarians enjoy so I regularly bring it to parties. I use rice crackers instead of bread because they don't get soggy as quickly. I also use the light Philadelphia Dill Cream Cheese spread instead of the mayo mixture. This makes preparation even quicker and easier.

I have made this several times and have used 2 different dressing mixes. The good seasons is perfect with a full packet but the wishbone is too strong if you use the entire pouch. Thought I'd throw that in as I see in some reviews members say to cut back on the seasoning mix. I only make it on super fresh baguette bread and with fresh dill...yum!
I agree to mix the spread a day ahead as it tastes better the next day. Thank you Dianne!

This is a great base recipe. I improve it with a few modifications. Instead of mayo I use miracle whip. I mix some dill in the mix. I put the mix on the bread. I use different kinds of breads. After putting the creamy mix on the bread, I cover it with mozzarella cheese. Pop it in the oven and broil it until the cheese start to melt. Then put the cucumber and dill on top before serving. YUMMY!

Enjoyed by all at Bible Study. I used 8 oz of Whole Foods Cream cheese with garlic and chives with 1/3 cup of mayo (may use sour cream in place of mayo). To this mixture I added:
only 1 teaspoon of dill. 
1/2 packet of good seasons Italian all natural salad dressing mix. 
1 green onion (green & white parts) thinly sliced with kitchen sheers. 
Mix these ingredients together and spread on sliced rounds of baguette bread that have been toasted toast in oven for 8 minutes at 375 degrees. This keeps the bread from getting soggy. Top with very thin slices of English (seedless) cucumbers.

This recipe was a big hit at our party. A Norwegian friend thought it was a Scandinavian recipe and Indian friends thought it reminded them of an Indian recipe. I agree that adding the seasoning to taste is a good idea. Used dried dill in the cream cheese and fresh dill sprigs as garnish. Served on a chilled platter.

Wonderfully refreshing flavor with the chilled cucumber and easy to make. I did toast the banquettes though and that provided a non-soggy/crisp that I think it needed. I tried it without mayo after reading previous reviews, but added it after finding the cream cheese to be too heavy alone. Added hellmans olive oil mayonnaise and the texture and taste was creamier and had that little extra that it needed. I took it to a party that I didn't know was catered, everyone was asking catered for the recipe, lol.

TOP SHELF..If you want to impress someone with a recipe this one is the one as YOU WILL impress your guest with this recipe. I made it as directions stated. As other reviewers said the entire package of Italian dressing to some may be too much, so taste as you mix this together. We VERY much enjoyed the blend it made using the entire package of dressing along with Hellmann's real mayonnaise. Slice the cucumber very thin lengthwise to get a little curl. If you have dried fresh dill it adds a wonderful essence to the flavor. (If you grow your own dill you will want to dry some for this recipe in the future) Use a fresh baguette for best results and cut it on a slight angle. Take along copies of this recipe as YOU WILL be asked for copies of it.

So I did do some changes, opted for sour cream instead of mayo and put the S&P in the cream cheese mixture along with the dill. Sliced a french loaf on a bias and toasted it in a pan with butter. Was really good assembled, even better when I drizzled balsamic vinegar on the bread then spread the mixture topped off with the thinly sliced cucumber (which I just used a peeler to make the slices)
I made it exactly as the recipe suggested and found the Italian -style dry salad mix made it WAY to salty. I would make again and omit the salad dressing or cut it in 1/2.

Super easy recipe! I substituted Greek yogurt for the mayo. It made a much thicker and richer spread. Definitely let the spread set overnight to let the flavors settle. This will definitely be a staple in this house! Use a food peeler for the cucumber. The presentation is gorgeous!
We all love this recipe. Agree with others to make spread enough ahead of time for flavors to meld. I use Triscuit dill and sea salt crackers with this. So good!
An easy delicious appetizer.. I & my friends loved it.

I have made this recipe for years. It's a recipe that everyone loves and I seldom take home leftovers. I do make these up about 4-5 hours ahead of time so that the flavors have a chance to blend. I did add the mayo but will leave out the next time. My original recipe calls for making these on cocktail rye bread & does not call for the mayo. I do like using the rye but have trouble finding in the South unless it's Christmas time. If using a baguette, make sure you buy a good quality dense loaf.
Everybody loved them so happy I found this recipe
Perfect
It was way too strong/salty, so added 1/4c mayo and 4oz cream cheese and more dill. Love it!
I used dill, crazy salt and Italian seasoning added to cream cheese
